question: Why do the shoes that go with Gladias's robe slow him down when he has to run?
answer_fact: They have heels to match other robe wearers' height and uneven soles to randomize how he walks.

question: Once the kids go off to Vil and Daia, what is Seila planning to do with her time?
answer_fact: She plans to spend a month or two in Freetown, visit Jahn, and gather material for a blog post on the United Cities.

question: Which menu number does Gladias usually order from the Dzego food truck?
answer_fact: He orders number ten, the same as usual.

question: During the thermodynamics lesson, why did Zei keep his Arctic Emperor joke to himself?
answer_fact: Spelling out such an obvious joke is poor form, and most of the class was likely already thinking it.

question: What did the instructor say was wrong with Zei's arm after the attack on the class?
answer_fact: His scan suggested a broken bone, and he told Zei to go to the hospital that same day.

question: How did Zei place in the Minpentai game he played the night before the bombing?
answer_fact: He came third, using a wall that bounced the opponents' gliders back at them.

question: How did Mov manage to find Gladias when lots of people nearby were wearing identical robes?
answer_fact: Gladias had left Mov on his trust list, so his AI turned on location sharing with Mov for their planned meeting day.

question: What first got Gladias interested in working on Steering?
answer_fact: Writing an alternative client for Silverchat, whose open API existed thanks to openness taxes, inspired him to give back.

question: According to Mov, why does the tax system go to such lengths to keep Keepers anonymous?
answer_fact: A Keeper whose views became public saw her husband lose his job days later amid Bluewhale's campaign, showing the risk of exposure.

question: What is the giant pyramid at the southern edge of Pafogai Du really, and what is it used for?
answer_fact: It's an existing mountain dressed up as a pyramid, its caves turned into offices and homes housing government departments and big businesses.

question: Why does Zei say a shield that can never be destroyed can't exist?
answer_fact: Physics is time-reversible, so whatever can be built can be undone by reversing the steps; every shield must have a weakness.

question: What does Mu caution Zei about just before the quarter-finals?
answer_fact: That he'll be on a team now and isn't a natural diplomat; live coordination with teammates will matter a lot.

question: Watching the quarter-final from far away, what does Fin think Zei wants almost as much as winning?
answer_fact: Fin believes Zei wants to hear Bai plead with him for help.

question: After the game, when Bai apologizes, what does Zei ask her for?
answer_fact: He asks to come along on her next Redshire vacation, then quickly adds his mom too.

question: Why can't Dzego just build its own all-seeing camera network to counter the Arctic surveillance?
answer_fact: Arctic spies are inside Dzego's agencies, so an all-seeing network would become their weapon; cameras instead reveal only suspicious data.

question: How is the entrance fee worked out at the economics institute Zei and Bai visit in Freetown?
answer_fact: It rises with the square root of time spent inside and falls as your academic or intellectual reputation score rises.

question: What kind of project does Seila suggest Gladias could take on if he becomes a Keeper?
answer_fact: Changing or creating rubrics so companies' products help Dzego more, since current rubrics don't.

question: Why did the priests let each player see what the other player's AI was thinking during the city final?
answer_fact: Mu says they wanted it closer to real life, where success depends on concealing your thinking, sometimes even from allies.

question: Why didn't Nine believe the bug hidden in the booth table was planted to spy on the Keepers?
answer_fact: Such bugs usually target careless businesses for market tips; Keepers hear only one of three groups and talk digitally through neck bands.

question: Why does Dzego disguise its training of future defenders as a game instead of just recruiting soldiers openly?
answer_fact: Any open military effort would be targeted by the Arctics; the game is safe only because it looks like mere sport.

question: Why did Gladias stop chasing perfect marks at school?
answer_fact: After a year of near-perfect grades he felt mostly fear of ruining his record, so he decided it wasn't worth it.

question: According to Eighteen, why does publishing military-relevant designs openly matter so much for Dzego?
answer_fact: Dzego can't invent top-end tech itself but excels at adapting open designs, as with secure software that protected it from Arctic sabotage.

question: What did Zei, Fin and Bai see on their way up the mountain to the city final?
answer_fact: An explosion and smoke cloud at the city's biggest chip factory, which Zei suspected was Arctic sabotage.

question: What did Vil offer Lily as a reward for doing better in civics?
answer_fact: If she scores over 75 on her next civics test, Vil will take her on his next trip to Northglade.

question: After his attack fell apart, how did Zei manage to come back and win the city final?
answer_fact: He had his AI build a factory with sixteen possible plans, secretly triggered by his own gliders, launching a surprise attack from mid-north.

question: What did the Freetown charging companies do to the carmaker that refused to chip in for defense?
answer_fact: They threatened to block Mogna's cars from about 90% of Freetown's chargers, and Mogna gave in the next day.

question: How can Den's hand device tell that a gadget answering it is really nearby and not relaying answers from somewhere else?
answer_fact: It pings the device a million times and requires replies within a tenth of a tick, limiting distance to about thirteen meters.

question: How does the network Den showed Zei hide who sent a message?
answer_fact: Messages are wrapped in three encryption layers peeled by randomly chosen nodes, so unmasking a sender needs three random nodes colluding.

question: If payments in Veridia are private, how does the government make sure shops actually pay sales tax?
answer_fact: Tax is sent automatically in real time, and enforcement relies on random inspectors ordering and checking a taxed payment type is used.

question: Who was the teenage girl sitting next to Gladias at the citizens' assembly, and what does she want to do?
answer_fact: Pelae, an older teen, who has decided to go into chemistry despite friends warning it will be hard.

question: What kind things had Lily done for the family that Gladias reminded her of when she was upset?
answer_fact: She baked Seila a birthday cake and brought Hreda food daily for a month after Hreda's accident.

question: How does Bai really feel about the way Zei beat her in the final?
answer_fact: She admires his tactics as beautiful, cleverer than her own trap, and wants to understand how he and Fin think.

question: What was the name of the Herald who led the citizens' assembly on public spaces?
answer_fact: Alagael, who had been a Herald for seven years.

question: What score did Lily get on the civics test she failed?
answer_fact: 59 percent, the third-worst result in her class.

question: Why would Bluewhale secretly pay people to donate to a project it didn't even own?
answer_fact: Its aim was to drain money from anything tied to open platforms, so the closed ecosystem would win by default.

question: Before the semifinal, why does Bai tell Zei not to hurry?
answer_fact: She noticed every other player, especially Gun, is too eager to win fast, rushing even when the scoring no longer rewards it.

question: Why does Gladias tell Delwart he doesn't expect the Arctics to escalate, when he isn't sure?
answer_fact: He feared it might happen, but admitting it would earn him a long lecture from Delwart about his biased sources.

question: Why didn't teaming three bots up against Zei on the train help them much?
answer_fact: That style of play wasn't in their training data, so they made basic errors and ate into each other's negentropy.

question: Why does Den send Zei back to Pafogai Du after the invasion?
answer_fact: The cryptographic infrastructure Dzego needs for secure coordination is run from Pafogai Du, and Den will tell him whom to contact.

question: What interrupted the family dinner at the restaurant, and how did Seila react?
answer_fact: A message from Lord Ephelion took over the screen showing Helisport, and Seila got up to unplug the screen herself.

question: What advice did Zei pass along for the Arctic soldier smuggling messages?
answer_fact: Train a model on the data, split bits into random buckets that must XOR to the message, and flip the most natural-looking bit.

question: How did Deluin beat Kau in the other semifinal?
answer_fact: He built no mobile ships, just walled himself in using nearby rock resources and reflected Kau's glider storms until Kau was overwhelmed.

question: What did Mov find out when he followed Delwart after the overheard meeting?
answer_fact: Two more meetings: one with a robed stranger about Silverchat, one with a Keeper about Dreadknot; then Delwart's trail went cold.

question: How does the championship keep a player from finding out the day's rule change before their match?
answer_fact: Players wait about a longhour in a room with no internet, and their hand devices and watches are collected.

question: How do the shrines work in the semifinal version of Minpentai?
answer_fact: Every thousand turns, changes inside a shrine are XORed onto areas near its corners, then the shrine resets to a default rock.

question: How do Keepers in a meeting keep each other from knowing who they are?
answer_fact: They hide their faces and speak through neck bands that output a freshly randomized AI-generated voice.

question: Who is the woman who greets Zei at the train station in the capital?
answer_fact: Su, an older Minpentai priest and one of the organizers of the national championship.

question: How did Bai gather her information on the other championship players?
answer_fact: She watched every game, befriended some players, and joined their practice sessions; nothing illicit.

question: What room was Zei given at his hotel in Sadzu Du?
answer_fact: Room 304; his reputation was over 150, so he didn't need to pay.

question: In the bottled water ad Gladias walks past, how much heavy water does the brand claim its water has?
answer_fact: Hydrafill claims 132 parts per million, versus 145 on average for competitors.
